This year can be said to be the year of the super app. OpenAI recently launched its own super app and admitted that the app is "a little chaotic." At the same time, Microsoft's CEO has also confirmed that a Copilot super app will be launched in the near future.

Microsoft Copilot "super app" will integrate Cowork, chat, coding and other features

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that combines Copilot chat, coding, and intelligent agent features. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said on Wednesday's earnings call that the app will launch within the year and will cover "consumer and commercial experiences." Nadella pointed out: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat functionality to Cowork and even Autopilots. This quarter, we will integrate various Copilot experiences, including coding, into a single super app... This is a major step forward, and I look forward to sharing more details with everyone later."

OpenAI's launch of its own "super app" turned into a disaster. But apparently it did not stop other companies from following this super app route.

Perhaps Microsoft can better build a multi-functional app and avoid repeating OpenAI's mistakes.

That said, CEO Satya Nadella recently also said that the company is shifting its focus from apps to intelligent agents. The AI era is still in its early stages, and the trends and best practices for building AI-driven interfaces are still evolving.

As for Apple, there is no indication that it is moving toward the super app direction; instead, it continues to launch independent and specialised new apps. Whether this strategy will change in the future remains to be seen.

What do you think of the recent "super app" boom? Feel free to tell us in the comments section.
